chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ruba'i ibn Abdallah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is for the scholar – if he is asked something of which he does not know – to say: 'Allāh is more knowing' and it is not for other than the scholar to say that.

key_terms.اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ: Allāh is more knowing (a phrase of humility and acknowledgment of divine omniscience)

ai.seo_question: What should a scholar say when he does not know the answer to a question?
ai.summary: This hadith delineates the protocol of 'Iqar' (acknowledging ignorance) specifically for the 'alim, establishing that saying 'Allāh a'lam' is a mark of scholarly humility and precision rather than mere admission of lack of knowledge. It cautions against the layperson appropriating this phrase, as it implies a level of authoritative judgment reserved for those trained in the sciences, thereby preserving the integrity of religious discourse. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on the specialized role of the scholar in deriving and conveying rulings.
